The order, issued under the Punjab Employees Efficiency, Discipline and Accountability (Peeda) Act 2006, accuses the BS-20 officer of abusing his authority by facilitating the illegal allotment of Unit-54, a house reserved for the Khateeb of Jamia Masjid, Neela Gumbad, to one Shahid Ishaq, son of retired provincial Khateeb Mufti Muhammad Ishaq Saqi, in Dec 2023 despite knowing the house’s reserved status and that it could not be allotted to any private person.

Dr Bukhari allegedly pressured field officers to submit favourable reports and later concealed material facts during high-level official meetings, ultimately resulting in a massive financial loss of Rs8.162m to the exchequer as compensation was paid out against the state property.

Ordering initiation of disciplinary proceedings against the accused under the Peeda Act 2006, the Punjab chief minister, acting as competent authority, appointed Punjab Planning and Development Board (P&DB) Chairman Dr Naeem Rauf as inquiry officer to proceed against the accused officer in terms of Section 5(1)(b) read with Section 9 of the Act ibid.
The inquiry officer has been asked to submit his report and recommendations to the Auqaf department secretary within 60 days of the initiation of inquiry.

The order says an application was submitted by a private person, Shahid Ishaq, son of Mr Ishaq Saqi (ex-provincial Khateeb) to the Auqaf secretary/chief administrator on Dec 19, 2023, for allotment of the house (Unit 54) attached to Jamia Masjid, Neela Gumbad, which was actually reserved for Khateeb of the mosque. At that time too, the house was under illegal occupation of Ishaq Saqi, who was residing there even after his retirement on April 1, 2019.

Instead of calling the report based on facts, the order says, Dr Bukhari pressurised the zonal administrator of Auqaf, Lahore (West), to submit a report in the favour of the applicant by writing the comments: “Hasb-e-Istada Karwai ho” in spite of having knowledge that no Khateeb house could be allotted to any private person, which is tantamount to corruption, inefficiency and misconduct under the provisions of Peeda Act 2006.

The order says, on the accused officer’s direction, the Lahore ex-zonal administrator submitted his report in favour of this illegal allotment on Dec 23, 2023. With active connivance of field officers– manager circle 2, Lahore, and zonal administrator, Lahore West – the former secretary, who was in close contact with Mufti Ishaq Saqi, allotted the reserved house illegally to a private person on Dec 28, 2023, the order says.

As per the order, the former secretary’s representative, Khalid Mehmood Sandhu, ex-director (Estate), attended a meeting, chaired by the then Local Govt and Community Development (LG&CD) department secretary, regarding payment of compensation to the affected persons of Neela Gumbad project on Aug 29, 2025. However, Mr Sandhu deliberately did not mention during the meeting that compensation of the said house could not be made to the illegal allottee, for it being a reserved house.

“Minutes of the 29th meeting of Provincial Cabinet held on Oct 06, 2025, transpire vide para 102.5 and 102.6 that you deliberately did not mention there that compensation of the said house cannot be made to the illegal allottee,” the order says.

Besides allotting the house illegally, the former secretary also caused a huge loss of Rs8.162m to the exchequer, as the amount was paid as compensation for the house to Shahid Ishaq, which is tantamount to corruption, inefficiency and misconduct under the Peeda Act, 2006.
The government has asked the accused former secretary to submit his written defence to the inquiry officer within seven days of the date of receipt of this order.
As both Dr Bukhari and Khalid Sandhu are also accused of financial irregularities in public funds, the order recommends recovery of around Rs34m from them.
After approval of the chief secretary, Senior Member Board of Revenue (SMBR) Nabeel Javed, in April 2026, was entrusted with the task to conduct a probe into the allegations against the two officers.
Earlier, responding to a Dawn query about the status of the probe against the two officers, Mr Javed had said it was “in process”.

Meanwhile, the Auqaf department has appointed Deputy Director (Admin) Azeem Hayat as departmental representative, allowing the accused officers to consult the record on which the aforesaid charges are based, if he desires so, within seven days of the receipt of the order.
Published in Dawn, November 2nd, 2026

headline: Auto parts industry in panic over New Energy Vehicle policy
description: Concerns among 1,200 manufacturers; policy gives six major shocks to the domestic industry.
author: Aamir Allawala
article_text:
The Auto and Auto Parts Policy 2026-31 has turned into a mystery. Multiple drafts are circulating, yet no one outside close government circles knows the exact contents of the document, which was approved “in principle” by Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif in early September and forwarded for “IMF review” late last month.

The country’s 1,200 auto parts manufacturing companies, which employ 300,000 people directly and 1.8 million indirectly, are in a state of panic after reading multiple leaked drafts. The latest draft begins by acknowledging the scale of the sector, noting $4 billion in foreign and domestic investment and domestic production valued at $6bn in 2026. The sector constitutes 4.5 per cent of the nation’s large-scale manufacturing, features more than 13 car assemblers, supports 1,200 auto parts manufacturers, and contributes Rs600bn in annual tax revenues.

The draft highlights three significant structural challenges. First is a distinct lack of domestic parts integration in New Energy Vehicles (NEVs) and vehicles introduced since 2016. Second is that export revenues have stagnated at just $190m. Third is a severe structural “cost of production” disadvantage relative to regional peers.

The draft celebrates a 40pc year-on-year increase in units produced. However, it fails to recognise that overall domestic demand is still lower than it was 20 years ago. For comparison, Indonesian auto demand grew by 279pc over 11 years from 318,367 units in 2003 to 1.21m units in 2014 on the back of an improved security situation after the 2002 Bali bombing, stable GDP growth, and enhanced consumer buying power.

Concerns among 1,200 manufacturers; policy gives six major shocks to the domestic industry

To address these hurdles, the draft outlines several key objectives: growing exports through integration into Global Value Chains (GVCs), promoting NEV adoption, lowering automobile prices, improving quality, protecting consumer interests, encouraging innovation through competition, and increasing transparency. The document boasts of benchmarking these proposals against peer states, emphasising a sharp reduction in tariffs to bring Pakistan’s overall weighted average tariff below 6pc by 2030. Finally, it claims a focus on increasing local value addition to reduce imports, especially for parts where the technology is already available domestically.

While the stated intentions are noble, the actual proposed measures completely contradict the objectives. The policy presents six major shocks to the domestic industry. The first shock is aggressive Completely Built Unit (CBU) duty cuts. The CBU import duties will progressively drop to 15pc by 2031. This defies all regional benchmarks; India’s CBU duty stands at 120pc, Thailand’s at 80pc, and Indonesia’s at 52pc. A tariff cut of this magnitude will trigger massive imports at the expense of domestic assemblers, worsening unemployment and straining Pakistan’s current account.

The second shock is subsidised NEV imports. Import duties on CBUs priced under $15,000 will be reduced to a mere 5pc. This is compounded by incredibly low sales taxes: 1pc on Battery Electric Vehicles (BEVs), 6pc on Range-Extended Electric Vehicles (REEVs), and 9pc on Plug-in Hybrid Electric Vehicles (PHEVs). Subsidising CBU imports directly conflicts with the goal of domestic industrialisation. A $15,000 car may be entry-level by global standards, but at over Rs4m it is out of reach for the vast majority of Pakistani households. The government will therefore sacrifice vital tax revenue to lower vehicle prices for a small, affluent minority, while simultaneously putting low-income factory workers out of jobs in a country where 40pc of the population lives below the poverty line.

The third shock is the phasing out of localised Internal Combustion Engine (ICE) parts. Import duties on existing, localised parts for conventional ICE vehicles will plummet from 46pc to 30pc in 2026-27, and down to 15pc by 2030–31. This means local manufacturers of auto parts who already operate at a 34pc structural cost disadvantage, will face extinction, wiping out billions in plant investments and hundreds of thousands of livelihoods.

The fourth shock is the blocking of future localisation. Tariffs on non-localised conventional ICE parts will drop from 30pc to 10pc (2026-27) and then to 5pc by 2030–31. By making imports this cheap, the government will permanently close the door on the local development of high-tech components like speedometers, automotive electronics, and engine/transmission parts.

The fifth shock is the disincentivising of NEV localisation. For NEV assemblers, locally produced parts that are common to both ICE vehicles and NEVs will carry a 20pc import duty. This makes local manufacturing financially unfeasible as assemblers will simply import them as part of Completely Knocked-Down (CKD) kits. Meanwhile, non-localised NEV-specific parts will face a mere 1pc customs duty, eliminating any incentive for future investment in domestic EV batteries, controllers, motors, or other new technologies.

The sixth and final shock is weak domestic value addition requirements for NEV assemblers. The Minimum Domestic Value Addition Requirement (MDVAR) for NEVs has been set at half the rate of conventional ICE vehicles. Specifically, the MDVAR for NEV Original Equipment Manufacturers (OEMs) is set at only 10pc for the first two years, 15pc for the third and fourth year, and 20pc for the fifth year of the life of the policy. As NEVs inevitably capture market share, this low threshold ensures assemblers will bypass domestic vendors entirely.

To summarise, the government’s stated intentions are correct. But the execution is deeply flawed. Historical evidence shows that policy mismatches damage localisation. Post-2016, localisation levels dropped because the government allowed new entrants to import localised parts at a concessionary 25pc customs duty. Conversely, older OEMs operating under stricter pre-2016 rules and at a 45pc tariff successfully achieved local value addition of 50pc to 65pc by value while keeping car prices lower than in Thailand, Indonesia and Malaysia (net of taxes).

If the current drafts are implemented without alignment, the country risks destroying its local industry and creating mass unemployment in pursuit of cheap imports. To achieve a competitive domestic auto industry with up to 50pc local content, Pakistan Association of Automotive Parts & Accessories Manufacturers sent its recommendations to the government in August.

The proposed tariff formula is based on 2007-2016 experience which showed that localisation required CBU import duties at minimum 50pc, localised parts (ICE & NEV) at minimum 40pc and non-localised parts (ICE & NEV) at minimum 30pc.

Any tariff structure below these thresholds risks permanently dismantling the domestic industrial infrastructure and wiping out the skilled jobs built in Pakistan over decades of painstaking effort.

The writer is a former chairman of PAPAAM

The first shock is aggressive Completely Built Unit (CBU) duty cuts. The CBU import duties will progressively drop to 15pc by 2031. This defies all regional benchmarks; India’s CBU duty stands at 120pc, Thailand’s at 80pc, and Indonesia’s at 52pc. A tariff cut of this magnitude will trigger massive imports at the expense of domestic assemblers, worsening unemployment and straining Pakistan’s current account.

The second shock is subsidised NEV imports. Import duties on CBUs priced under $15,000 will be reduced to a mere 5pc. This is compounded by incredibly low sales taxes: 1pc on Battery Electric Vehicles (BEVs), 6pc on Range-Extended Electric Vehicles (REEVs), and 9pc on Plug-in Hybrid Electric Vehicles (PHEVs). Subsidising CBU imports directly conflicts with the goal of domestic industrialisation. A $15,000 car may be entry-level by global standards, but at over Rs4m it is out of reach for the vast majority of Pakistani households. The government will therefore sacrifice vital tax revenue to lower vehicle prices for a small, affluent minority, while simultaneously putting low-income factory workers out of jobs in a country where 40pc of the population lives below the poverty line.

The third shock is the phasing out of localised Internal Combustion Engine (ICE) parts. Import duties on existing, localised parts for conventional ICE vehicles will plummet from 46pc to 30pc in 2026-27, and down to 15pc by 2030–31. This means local manufacturers of auto parts who already operate at a 34pc structural cost disadvantage, will face extinction, wiping out billions in plant investments and hundreds of thousands of livelihoods.

The fourth shock is the blocking of future localisation. Tariffs on non-localised conventional ICE parts will drop from 30pc to 10pc (2026-27) and then to 5pc by 2030–31. By making imports this cheap, the government will permanently close the door on the local development of high-tech components like speedometers, automotive electronics, and engine/transmission parts.

The fifth shock is the disincentivising of NEV localisation. For NEV assemblers, locally produced parts that are common to both ICE vehicles and NEVs will carry a 20pc import duty. This makes local manufacturing financially unfeasible as assemblers will simply import them as part of Completely Knocked-Down (CKD) kits. Meanwhile, non-localised NEV-specific parts will face a mere 1pc customs duty, eliminating any incentive for future investment in domestic EV batteries, controllers, motors, or other new technologies.

The sixth and final shock is weak domestic value addition requirements for NEV assemblers. The Minimum Domestic Value Addition Requirement (MDVAR) for NEVs has been set at half the rate of conventional ICE vehicles. Specifically, the MDVAR for NEV Original Equipment Manufacturers (OEMs) is set at only 10pc for the first two years, 15pc for the third and fourth year, and 20pc for the fifth year of the life of the policy. As NEVs inevitably capture market share, this low threshold ensures assemblers will bypass domestic vendors entirely.

To summarise, the government’s stated intentions are correct. But the execution is deeply flawed. Historical evidence shows that policy mismatches damage localisation. Post-2016, localisation levels dropped because the government allowed new entrants to import localised parts at a concessionary 25pc customs duty. Conversely, older OEMs operating under stricter pre-2016 rules and at a 45pc tariff successfully achieved local value addition of 50pc to 65pc by value while keeping car prices lower than in Thailand, Indonesia and Malaysia (net of taxes).

If the current drafts are implemented without alignment, the country risks destroying its local industry and creating mass unemployment in pursuit of cheap imports. To achieve a competitive domestic auto industry with up to 50pc local content, Pakistan Association of Automotive Parts & Accessories Manufacturers sent its recommendations to the government in August.

The proposed tariff formula is based on 2007-2016 experience which showed that localisation required CBU import duties at minimum 50pc, localised parts (ICE & NEV) at minimum 40pc and non-localised parts (ICE & NEV) at minimum 30pc.

Any tariff structure below these thresholds risks permanently dismantling the domestic industrial infrastructure and wiping out the skilled jobs built in Pakistan over decades of painstaking effort.

The writer is a former chairman of PAPAAM

headline: Factory worker dies, eight injured in gas cylinder blast in Lahore's Gulberg
description: The blast took place on the first floor of the Shezan Bakers factory where more than 40 employees were busy at work.
author: The Newspaper's Staff Reporter
article_text:
LAHORE: A worker died while his eight colleagues were injured, three of them critically, when a gas cylinder exploded in a factory on the Gurumangat Road, Gulberg, on Sunday.

The blast took place on the first floor of the Shezan Bakers factory where more than 40 employees were busy at work.

A spokesperson for Rescue 1122 said that as a result of the blast , a part of the building collapsed which occurred soon after leakage in the gas cylinder. He identified the deceased worker as Sajid (35) and added that rescuers shifted the injured to hospital.

Published in Dawn, November 2nd, 2026

headline: Oil prices ease 3pc on optimism for Qatari-led talks on ending Iran war
description: Oil prices slipped more than 3 per cent after Iranian and Qatari officials held a third straight day of talks aimed...
article_text:
Oil prices slipped more than 3 per cent after Iranian and Qatari officials held a third straight day of talks aimed at pushing for a deal to end the US-Israeli war on Iran.

Brent crude futures fell $3.68, or 3.2pc, to $109.75 a barrel while US West Texas Intermediate crude was at $100.69 a barrel, down $3.43, or 3.3pc.

Brent ended October at its highest in six months amid concerns that the US-Iran conflict could escalate again after Tuesday’s US midterm elections.

“Oil is seeing a technical pullback this morning after last weeks strong gains,” said Tim Waterer, chief market analyst at KCM Trade.

“Lingering hopes of some form of diplomatic progress, combined with the absence of any meaningful military escalation over the weekend, have taken some of the immediate heat out of prices for now.”

headline: Mobile phone shop owner hospitalised after ‘police torture’ in Kasur
description: Police register case against 40 shopkeepers for "attack".
author: Dawn Report
article_text:
KASUR: A mobile shop owner was hospitalised after being critically injured in alleged police torture at his shop in the Mobile Market, Railway Road, Kot Radha Kishan, the other day.

He was shifted to Lahore due to critical injuries.

Footage of the incident went viral on social media. It showed the shopkeeper, identified as Yousaf, in the chokehold of an assistant sub-inspector (ASI) behind the showcases of his shop. A group of traders is seen arguing with the policemen and protesting against the torture that had caused a head injury to the shopkeeper.

The shopkeeper was allegedly injured by the strikes of the butt of a gun during the raid.

Police register case against 40 shopkeepers for ‘attack’

The police wanted to take the shopkeeper away for investigation in a case but he refused to go with them, fearing his arrest, saying that he would himself come to the police station to join the investigation.

The police didn’t agree and allegedly tortured him. Hearing his hue and cry, other traders also gathered at this shop and protested against the police torture. They shifted him to hospital in critical condition.

However, on Sunday, Kot Radha Kishan police booked 40 suspects, 15 of them nominated, on charges of attacking police, tearing off their uniform, snatching cash and getting the suspect (shopkeeper) released from custody. The footage did not show any such happening.

The police FIR alleged that the suspect, Yousaf, was a member of Badho Meo Gang involved in pickpocketing and mobile snatching incidents. He had a mobile phone shop and would allegedly buy and sell snatched mobile phones after changing their IMEIs to conceal their identity.

According to the police allegations, on the disclosure of a suspected mobile snatcher and pickpocket, Ali Haider of Pattoki, Shaikhum police raided the shop of Yousaf who put up resistance, injured himself by breaking the glass showcases in the shop and tried to die by suicide. The suspect also raised hue and cry that alarmed other people who rushed his shop and got him released from custody.

Rescue 1122 shifted Yousaf to the Tehsil Headquarters Hospital, Kot Radha Kishan, in an injured condition where the doctors referred him to Lahore in a critical condition.

The video of the incident also went viral on social media. On Sunday, police lodged a case against 40 suspects on the complaint of Shaikhum SHO Raheel Ahmed.

Published in Dawn, November 2nd, 2026

The police wanted to take the shopkeeper away for investigation in a case but he refused to go with them, fearing his arrest, saying that he would himself come to the police station to join the investigation.

The police didn’t agree and allegedly tortured him. Hearing his hue and cry, other traders also gathered at this shop and protested against the police torture. They shifted him to hospital in critical condition.

headline: Man kills wife, injures five children with knife in Lahore
description: A police official says the incident took place at Hakim Chowk where the suspect had a quarrel with his wife over some domestic issue.
author: The Newspaper's Staff Reporter
article_text:
LAHORE: A man allegedly killed his wife and injured their five children, attacking them with a knife, in the jurisdiction of Nishtar Colony police here on Sunday.

Identified as Arshad, the suspect was arrested by the police and booked for murder.

A police official says the incident took place at Hakim Chowk where the suspect had a quarrel with his wife over some domestic issue a couple of days back. After the quarrel, his wife, along with their five children, went to his parents’ house.

On Sunday, he says, Arshad went to his in-laws’ house to bring his wife and children back, but she refused to return.

Annoyed by her refusal, the suspect attacked his wife with a knife and also injured the children when they tried to rescue their mother. The woman was critically injured in the attack.

The police rushed to the spot, along with the Rescue 1122 officials, on being informed about the incident.

The Rescue 1122 staff shifted the injured woman and children to the hospital. Later, the woman succumbed to her wounds at the hospital, while the condition of one of the children is also stated to be serious.

ENCOUNTER: A suspect was allegedly killed during an alleged encounter with the police in Shahdara Town here on Sunday.

The police claimed the suspect was shot dead ‘in the firing of his own accomplices’ when he was being taken by a team for the recovery of a pistol he had allegedly used in criminal activities.

Identified as Arshad, the suspect was allegedly involved in many theft and robbery cases, according to the police.

A police official claims that as the police and the suspect reached near Ravi Road, four armed men allegedly opened indiscriminate fire on the police to rescue him.

The police returned the fire and after the crossfire, the suspect was allegedly found dead. A constable, Farooq, also got injured during the encounter, he adds.

Police teams have been dispatched to trace and arrest the fleeing attackers, while the body was shifted to the city morgue for an autopsy.

headline: Some respite in Sisyphean quest to end polio in Karachi
description: Through small lunches and Qinqi rickshaws, District Central administration helps make the enormous task of vaccinating thousands.
author: Shazia Hasan
article_text:
KARACHI: They are foot soldiers. Their only weapon: polio drops in a small blue icebox with an ice pack to keep the vaccine cool, even though they themselves may be sweating and exhausted in the scorching heat.

These health workers (mostly women as they are allowed inside homes) fight for the eradication of polio in Pakistan, one of only two polio-endemic countries in the world alongside Afghanistan. Sadly, in both Pakistan and Afghanistan, the fight against the crippling disease has run into rumours and misinformation, especially among the uneducated. Many not just refuse to let their children receive the drops, they even turn violent if shown some sense.

And yet in the face of all adversity the women carry on with their duty. From 8am to 5pm, they walk miles as they go door to door asking if there is any child there under the age of five to administer the drops to. Some 80 to 90 homes within a district are covered daily and the cycle must be repeated twice, even thrice sometimes, during a seven-day campaign. For safety reasons each team is also accompanied by a support team, including police and other personnel from the commissioner’s office and the Sindh government’s health department.

It was during such a campaign last year when in the field the Deputy Commissioner of District Central, Taha Saleem, heard of a problem that they had been overlooking while concentrating more on covering areas to administer vaccines, target number of children and the children missed because of family refusals.

Through small lunches and Qinqi rickshaws, District Central administration helps make the enormous task of vaccinating thousands of children less daunting

One of the polio workers quietly diverted his attention to the amount of walking they have to do while covering areas. Though her colleagues laughed it off, the deputy commissioner got thinking. There happened to be tens of thousands of homes in his district to be visited by around 4,000 polio workers who had to walk from eight to 10 kilometres daily to complete their task.

In order to arrive on duty at 8am, many of the workers left their homes before dawn, around 6am. And their work doesn’t usually finish precisely at 5pm. Realistically, it is 7pm as they update their data. The area supervisors who look after three to four teams even stay till 9pm. During this while they also barely ate even though their stipend of Rs1,500 per day included food and transportation allowance, which they would not spend to save money. So it came up to working for over 14 hours on an empty stomach.

Something had to be done. And it included food and transportation for the polio workers. Memorandums of Understanding (MoUs) were signed for this purpose with Saylani Welfare Trust and the Bohra Community for food and the Town Municipal Corporation for transportation.

In District Central now, from 1pm to 2pm lunch is supplied during campaigns and they are also provided with transport in the shape of seven- to nine-seater rickshaws or qinqis. The qinqis bring the workers to the field and they remain parked there until the workers are done. The drivers of these vehicles have each polio worker’s number, too, to make sure no one is missed while transporting them from here to there.

According to Taha Saleem, the little consideration shown to the polio workers has increased their turnover. “Since last year, when we started facilitating them, we have also been able to retain the workers. They have all returned this year,” he said.

Dr Aneel Kumar, who liaisons between the DC Office and the health department, said that thanks to transportation provided to the workers, they are also able to keep the vaccine fresh the entire day. “Their ice packs used to melt. But now they are able to go back to their facilitation centres to get fresh ice packs,” he said.

Kanwal Bashir, a polio worker, told Dawn that earlier to save money they used to have a samosa or a packet of chips, which would serve as lunch for them.

“But now we get to eat better. The transport also helps us replace our ice pack every three to four hours to keep the vaccine fresh,” she added.

The next polio campaign starts on Monday (today). The teams of polio workers of District Central are feeling motivated and ready to face all challenges that come their way.

Published in Dawn, November 2nd, 2026

Through small lunches and Qinqi rickshaws, District Central administration helps make the enormous task of vaccinating thousands of children less daunting

One of the polio workers quietly diverted his attention to the amount of walking they have to do while covering areas. Though her colleagues laughed it off, the deputy commissioner got thinking. There happened to be tens of thousands of homes in his district to be visited by around 4,000 polio workers who had to walk from eight to 10 kilometres daily to complete their task.

In order to arrive on duty at 8am, many of the workers left their homes before dawn, around 6am. And their work doesn’t usually finish precisely at 5pm. Realistically, it is 7pm as they update their data. The area supervisors who look after three to four teams even stay till 9pm. During this while they also barely ate even though their stipend of Rs1,500 per day included food and transportation allowance, which they would not spend to save money. So it came up to working for over 14 hours on an empty stomach.

Something had to be done. And it included food and transportation for the polio workers. Memorandums of Understanding (MoUs) were signed for this purpose with Saylani Welfare Trust and the Bohra Community for food and the Town Municipal Corporation for transportation.

In District Central now, from 1pm to 2pm lunch is supplied during campaigns and they are also provided with transport in the shape of seven- to nine-seater rickshaws or qinqis. The qinqis bring the workers to the field and they remain parked there until the workers are done. The drivers of these vehicles have each polio worker’s number, too, to make sure no one is missed while transporting them from here to there.

According to Taha Saleem, the little consideration shown to the polio workers has increased their turnover. “Since last year, when we started facilitating them, we have also been able to retain the workers. They have all returned this year,” he said.

Dr Aneel Kumar, who liaisons between the DC Office and the health department, said that thanks to transportation provided to the workers, they are also able to keep the vaccine fresh the entire day. “Their ice packs used to melt. But now they are able to go back to their facilitation centres to get fresh ice packs,” he said.

Kanwal Bashir, a polio worker, told Dawn that earlier to save money they used to have a samosa or a packet of chips, which would serve as lunch for them.

“But now we get to eat better. The transport also helps us replace our ice pack every three to four hours to keep the vaccine fresh,” she added.

The next polio campaign starts on Monday (today). The teams of polio workers of District Central are feeling motivated and ready to face all challenges that come their way.

headline: PPP stages rally against prolonged power, gas outages in Karachi's district South
description: MNA says meetings with K-Electric officials at the national and provincial assembly levels had failed to improve the utility’s performance or attitude towards consumers.
author: The Newspaper's Staff Reporter
article_text:
KARACHI: The Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP) on Sunday staged a protest rally from Lyari Gate to the Karachi Press Club against prolonged electricity and gas outages in Lyari and other areas of the city’s south district, warning that demonstrations would be held outside the headquarters of both utility providers if the situation was not addressed.

Led by PPP South District President Javed Nagori, the rally was attended by MNA Sardar Nabil Gabol, senior party leaders, local representatives, workers and a large number of women and residents from Lyari, Saddar, Burns Road, Garden and other affected neighbourhoods.

Addressing the protesters, MNA Gabol said meetings with K-Electric (KE) officials at the national and provincial assembly levels had failed to improve the utility’s performance or attitude towards consumers.

He vowed that the PPP would protest at every available forum alongside the South District organisation until KE and Sui Southern Gas Company (SSGC) corrected their practices.

The demonstrators raised slogans against both utility companies and demanded an end to prolonged electricity and gas outages.

Mr Nagori described prolonged power outages in Lyari as an act of high-handedness by KE, claiming that residents faced up to 16 hours of loadshedding daily, with outages reaching 21 hours in some localities.

He also criticised SSGC for failing to provide adequate gas despite collecting charges from consumers for newly laid pipelines across Karachi.

He said the Sindh government had distributed solar systems to thousands of households in line with PPP chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari’s announcement regarding 300 units of free electricity.

He demanded immediate government action against KE and warned that the protest movement would continue until public grievances were resolved.

headline: Five killed in fresh ethnic violence in India's Manipur
description: The predominantly Christian Kuki and Naga tribes have a long history of conflict over competing claims to ethnic homelands in the remote northeastern state.
author: Reuters
article_text:
NEW DELHI: Five people were killed in two separate incidents in India’s northeastern state of Manipur, police said on Sunday, as fresh ethnic violence erupted in the conflict-hit region.

Three men from the Kuki tribal group were killed in an exchange of gunfire between “unidentified armed miscreants” in the state’s Noney district on Saturday, according to a police statement.

The bodies of two other men from the same community, who had gone missing earlier this week, were recovered in Kangpokpi district on Sunday morning after security personnel launched a search operation, a second police statement said.

A top Kuki tribal body blamed Naga separatist ou­­t­­fits for the killings, desc­ribing them as a “direct unprovoked assault . . . in their homeland.” The killings came amid mass protests attended by hundreds of thousands of people in the state capital Imphal and other areas, demanding the abrogation of a ceasefire arrangement between Kuki armed gro­ups and the Indian state.

The predominantly Christian Kuki and Naga tribes have a long history of conflict over competing claims to ethnic homelands in the remote northeastern state. The latest fighting erupted after a Naga man was allegedly assaulted by men from the Kuki community in February this year.

The killing of three Kuki pastors in May, allegedly by Naga armed groups, triggered a series of retaliatory abductions and killings by both sides. The latest Kuki-Naga clashes have added to tensions in Manipur, where the Kuki community is also embroiled in a bloody ethnic conflict with the mainly Hindu Meitei community that began in May 2023 over economic benefits and job quotas.

headline: PIA engineer gunned down in suspected targeted attack in Karachi's Gulistan-i-Jauhar
description: The SHO has ruled out robbery, saying the exact motive would be ascertained after investigation.
author: The Newspaper's Staff Reporter
article_text:
KARACHI: An engineer working with the Pakistan International Airlines (PIA) was shot dead in a suspected targeted attack in Gulistan-i-Jauhar on Sunday afternoon, police and rescue services officials said.

Sharea Faisal SHO Anser Ahmed Butt said that Imtiaz Ahmed, 54, left his home in Block-13 to purchase bread when unidentified assailants riding a motorcycle targeted him and rode away.

He said three bullets hit a nearby parked car while one bullet hit him that proved fatal. He was shifted to a nearby private hospital where doctors pronounced him dead on arrival. Later, the body was shifted to the Jinnah Postgraduate Medical Centre for a post-mortem examination.

The SHO ruled out robbery, saying the exact motive would be ascertained after investigation.

He said the deceased was originally from Lahore and that police had contacted his brother, who was on his way to Karachi. Formal proceedings to ascertain the motive and identify the killers would be initiated after his arrival, he added.

He said the deceased’s wife was currently in Germany to visit their daughter.

Published in Dawn, November 2nd, 2026

Sharea Faisal SHO Anser Ahmed Butt said that Imtiaz Ahmed, 54, left his home in Block-13 to purchase bread when unidentified assailants riding a motorcycle targeted him and rode away.

He said three bullets hit a nearby parked car while one bullet hit him that proved fatal. He was shifted to a nearby private hospital where doctors pronounced him dead on arrival. Later, the body was shifted to the Jinnah Postgraduate Medical Centre for a post-mortem examination.

headline: Muttahida set to launch street movement for new administrative units
description: Khalid Maqbool announces rally on Sharea Faisal on Nov 29; calls for referendum to determine will of people on new provinces.
author: The Newspaper's Staff Reporter
article_text:
KARACHI: The Muttahida Qaumi Movement-Pakistan (MQM-P) has launched a major mobilisation campaign for the creation of new administrative units, with party chairman Dr Khalid Maqbool Siddiqui announcing on Sunday a “historic rally” on Sharea Faisal on Nov 29 as part of the movement’s push for constitutional and administrative reforms.

Addressing a workers’ convention held at KMC Park in PIB Colony, Dr Siddiqui said the time had come for the oppressed to unite against “an entrenched system of feudal domination and family-based politics.”

A large number of party activists, including women, attended the event. MQM-P leaders credited the success of their show to former Karachi Tanzeemi Committee in-charge Hammad Siddiqui, who they said was overseeing organisational affairs from behind the scenes.

However, senior leader Mustafa Kamal and his close aides were conspicuous by their absence.

Khalid Maqbool announces rally on Sharea Faisal on Nov 29; calls for referendum to determine will of people on new provinces

Dr Siddiqui, who is federal education minister, called for referendums under the Constitution to determine the will of the people on the creation of new administrative units in Sindh and the three other provinces.

He argued that the existing provincial structure had failed to deliver inclusive governance and equitable distribution of resources.

“The era of feudal democracy has run its course. The establishment of new administrative units has become the country’s destiny,” he said, adding that the Nov 29 rally would mark a significant step in the party’s campaign.

Dr Siddiqui said the party wanted political power and national resources to reach neighbourhoods and ordinary citizens rather than remain concentrated in the hands of influential families.

He said that a democratic system could not be considered representative if workers and ordinary people lacked a voice in parliament.

Responding to questions about the proposed province, he said the migrants who had come to Pakistan had sacrificed their properties in India for the sake of the new country.

Senior MQM-P leader Dr Farooq Sattar, addressing the gathering, said the existing four-province arrangement had become a mechanism for sustaining the dominance of a handful of political families.

He called for participatory and inclusive governance at the grassroots level, arguing that administrative restructuring was essential to address growing urban challenges and public grievances.

He also criticised the Pakistan Peoples Party for its mismanagement of Sindh over the past 18 years. He said that the proposed administrative units would not undermine Sindh’s cultural identity, adding that the party would continue to embrace Sindhi traditions, including the cap and ajrak.

Former Karachi mayor Wasim Akhtar urged workers to remain united under Dr Siddiqui’s leadership, saying the party’s supporters had stood by the organisation through difficult times.

The meeting was also attended by senior party leaders Syed Aminul Haque, Sindh Assembly Opposition Leader Ali Khurshidi, members of the party’s coordination committee, lawmakers and a large number of workers from district East.

Published in Dawn, November 2nd, 2026

headline: Rawalpindi Development Authority plans major road rehabilitation scheme
description: Work is expected to be complete in a year at a cost of Rs68.98 million, says official.
author: Aamir Yasin
article_text:
RAWALPINDI: After sitting idle for one year, the Rawalpindi Development Authority (RDA) has planned road rehabilitation and infrastructure improvement works in the garrison city at an estimated cost of Rs68.98 million.

A senior official of RDA told Dawn that in the last one year the civic agency was looking after Rawalpindi Ring Road project worth Rs47 billion, while no development work was launched for rehabilitation of roads.

He said that the Punjab government did not approve its two main projects -- Murree Road expansion from Committee Chowk to Chandni Chowk and repair of Murree Road from Faizabad to Marrir Chowk.

He said that the RDA submitted a plan to rehabilitate Ch. Bostan Khan Road from Chaklala Scheme-III to Lahore High Court Rawalpindi bench, but the local administration handed over the construction task to Punjab Highway Department.

Work is expected to be complete in a year at a cost of Rs68.98 million, says official

Apart from this, he said, it also planned to construct an underpass to connect I.J. Principal Road and Double Road at Shamsabad but it was also not approved. As a result, the civic agency started work on a commercial plaza and construction of flats for RDA employees.

He said that the new proposed development scheme, “Framework Agreement for Rehabilitation/Repair of Roads, Footpaths, Storm Water Drains, Manholes and Road Marking at Different Roads of City”, aims to address the repair and maintenance of urban road infrastructure.

Under the scheme, he said the scope of work included the rehabilitation and repair of roads, footpaths, storm water drains and manholes, along with marking on various roads across the city.

The estimated cost of the project is Rs68,983,836, including applicable taxes.

The stipulated completion period is 12 months.

The official said that the proposed works were intended to improve road conditions and maintain essential urban infrastructure, including drainage facilities and pedestrian pathways.

The repair and maintenance of these facilities are important for smoother traffic movement, pedestrian convenience and the effective drainage of rainwater.

However, he said a survey had been started to identify the roads for rehabilitation. He said that the old Airport Road and Rawal Road would be on the top priority as these required massive repair work.

He said the proposed scheme would be sent to the Punjab government for final approval and after getting the go-ahead signal PC-I will be prepared.

When contacted, RDA spokesman Mohammad Irfan confirmed that the civic agency plans to start work on the road development scheme.

Published in Dawn, November 2nd, 2026

headline: CM inaugurates Rs250m Sindhi Muslim Food Walk
description: Murad says organised commercial spaces can attract investment, generate employment and strengthen economic activity.
author: Dawn Report
article_text:
• Murad says organised commercial spaces can attract investment, generate employment and strengthen economic activity at neighbourhood level• Calls for regular maintenance, proper waste management, pedestrian safety and effective traffic management to keep the food walk attractive and functional

KARACHI: Sindh Chief Minister Syed Murad Ali Shah on Sunday evening inaugurated the Rs250 million Sindhi Muslim Food Walk in Chanesar Town, marking a major step towards transforming of one of Karachi’s popular commercial and food destinations into a more organised, attractive and pedestrian-friendly public space.

He also urged other town administrations to undertake similar initiatives through improved revenue generation and efficient utilisation of their financial resources.

According to an official statement, the urban improvement project aims to promote food and cultural tourism, facilitating local businesses, improving civic infrastructure and providing residents and visitors with a better environment to enjoy the city’s rich culinary culture.

Following the inauguration, the chief minister visited different eateries along the Food Walk, interacted with restaurant owners, customers and members of the public, and mingled with people enjoying the lively atmosphere.

He also obliged citizens by posing for selfies, turning the occasion into an opportunity for public interaction beyond the formal inauguration ceremony.

The visit underscored the importance of making public spaces more accessible and welcoming, while connecting urban development initiatives with the everyday lives of citizens.

Addressing the inauguration ceremony, he congratulated the Chanesar Town Municipal Corporation Chairman Farhan Ghani, municipal commissioner, engineers, contractors and workers who had contributed to the project’s completion.

The chief minister said Sindhi Muslim was already among Karachi’s well-known commercial and food destinations, attracting visitors from different parts of the city.

He said the Food Walk was not merely a beautification scheme but a comprehensive urban improvement initiative designed to make the area more accessible, attractive, organised and convenient for businesses, visitors and residents.

According to the statement, the development works include replacement of sewerage lines, installation of underground electrical cabling and removal of overhead wires, rehabilitation of roads and pedestrian footpaths, installation of modern streetlights, bollard lights and decorative lighting, plantation and landscaping, beautification of roundabouts, improvement of parking facilities and diversion roads, and installation of traffic signs and road markings.

Syed Murad Ali Shah said such improvements would enhance the experience of visitors and create a more organised environment for restaurants, shops and other businesses operating in the area.

Highlighting Karachi’s potential for food and cultural tourism, the chief minister said the city’s cuisine, traditions, diversity and hospitality were important elements of its identity. Initiatives such as the Sindhi Muslim Food Walk could help unlock this potential by creating opportunities for restaurants, small businesses, entrepreneurs, vendors and the local workforce.

He observed that better public infrastructure and organised commercial spaces could attract private investment, generate employment and strengthen economic activity at the neighbourhood level.

Published in Dawn, November 2nd, 2026

headline: 120 Swabi schools sealed over poor building conditions
description: The inspection campaign, covering both public and private schools, has been launched following the collapse of a private school building in Peshawar.
author: Muqaddam Khan
article_text:
SWABI: The district administration has sealed around 120 schools, mostly private, in different parts of Swabi after inspections revealed that their buildings were unsafe for students, sources said on Sunday.

The sources told Dawn that inspections conducted in all four tehsils of the district found cracks in the walls and rooms of several school buildings, making them unfit for educational activities and posing a threat to students’ lives.

The inspection teams sealed the institutions found to be dangerous, despite objections and excuses by some school administrations.

Officials made it clear that no compromise would be made on safety of students and took decisions on the spot after assessing the condition of the buildings, the sources said.

The inspection campaign, covering both public and private schools, was launched following the collapse of a private school building in Peshawar, which claimed the lives of 31 children and a female teacher.

Assistant commissioners of the four tehsils are leading the inspection teams and have been directed to complete the exercise without discrimination, giving priority to safety of students to prevent any untoward incident. When contacted, Deputy Commissioner Nasarullah Khan told Dawn that inspection would continue without interruption to check all schools in the district.

He said that out of approximately 2,000 public and private schools in Swabi, 1,224 had so far been inspected and around 120 sealed. The remaining institutions would be inspected soon, he added.

“We will not stop until we complete the task in accordance with the provincial government’s directives,” he said.

The deputy commissioner said the district had a total of 289,180 students, adding that the administration did not have separate figures for children enrolled in private schools. He said students of sealed public-sector schools would be accommodated in nearby educational institutions to ensure that their studies were not disrupted. Heads of the schools concerned had been directed to make immediate arrangements in this regard.

Similarly, private school administrations had been instructed to rent suitable alternative buildings and continue classes there while arranging repairs for their sealed premises.

They would be allowed to resume classes in their original buildings only after these had been renovated and cleared by the district administration, he added.

“We understand the importance of children’s education. We are taking urgent action to ensure that their education continues smoothly,” the deputy commissioner said.

headline: Jhelum's ancient Padhri village faces relentless erosion
description: The village is surrounded on all sides by deep ditches, making it inaccessible from almost every direction except through a narrow passage that provides road access.
author: Hamid Asghar
article_text:
Located at the foot of Tilla Jogian, Padhri village is another place dotted with astonishing examples of stone architecture typical of the Salt Range terrain.

Locally sourced stones have been crafted into remarkable structures, reflecting the enduring nature of art.

Padhri is a small village nestled among the hillocks beneath Tilla Jogian, a site dating back to the BC era.

Padhri is a purely Potohari word, mostly used for a stretch of land smoothed out from uneven terrain. The medium-sized village is spread across a small patch of land surrounded on all sides by deep ditches, making it inaccessible from almost every direction except through a narrow passage that provides road access.

The ordinary as well as palatial houses, which are now rapidly being demolished in the name of modernity, were built with stone. Even the remaining stretches of its streets offer a glimpse of an ancient Italian spectacle. This beautiful marvel of local stone architecture also bears the footprints of the harmonious coexistence of different religions and cultures.

A stone-built Hindu temple, with intact frescoes depicting deities and other designs, is now being used as a cattle pen. This reflects the neglect of our history and culture that is so common under the ‘bliss of ignorance’.

Muhammad Tariq, a local resident, told this correspondent that the shining brass masts once stood atop the temple but were stolen overnight about a decade ago.

Syed Ahmed, another resident, while guiding this correspondent through the streets, said all the houses had been built with grey stones brought from the surrounding hills of Tarakki, Domeli and Tilla Jogian. Hindus and Muslims lived there in complete harmony and communion. After the Partition of the subcontinent, the vacated houses were mostly allotted to migrants from Kashmir and other areas. Most of these allottees later sold the properties, while alterations to the buildings continued unchecked by the Evacuee Trust, which had allotted them.

A centuries-old small mosque, featuring a highly attractive facade built with sandy grey stones, is another marvel of stone craftsmanship in the Domeli and Tilla region. Its architecture has few parallels in modern construction and technology.

Chaudhary Sarmad Ehsan Sadiq, a visitor from a university in the United States, commenting on the precision of the intricate and complex designs, said this represented advanced architectural engineering that had flourished in the Domeli and Tilla Jogian region in particular.

The use of large, single stones as canvases to carve arches, pillars and panels with geometrical and artistic precision represented a remarkable science known only to the masons who had lived among these stones for generations around Tilla Jogian, Sarmad Ehsan said.

The remains of a beautifully constructed villa belonging to an influential figure of ancient times also stand surrounded by bushes. Its surviving series of magnificent arches resting on symmetrical pillars hints at the prestigious position it enjoyed during the British era and beyond.

Chaudhary Asim, a UK-based native of the area, regretted that unchecked soil erosion on all sides of Padhri village was undermining the foundations of houses.

“Eroding earth crumbling down into the surrounding ditches is endangering not only the population but also the centuries-old stone architecture, which is deteriorating day by day,” he said. He urged Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz Sharif to have the historic village declared a protected site by the Archaeology and Culture Department to prevent further destruction.

When contacted for comment, Jhelum Deputy Commissioner Mir Reza Ozgen acknowledged the seriousness of the situation and regretted the unavailability of funds. However, he said that an assessment and PC-I for the preservation of the monuments would be prepared, along with a formal request for the provision of funds.

Published in Dawn, November 2nd, 2026

headline: Islamabad's Capital Development Authority appoints three new directors general
description: Retired Brig Mohammad Javed Iqbal, retired Brig Rashid Manzoor and retired Brig Azhar Khan have been appointed as DGs.
author: Kashif Abbasi
article_text:
ISLAMABAD: The Capital Development Authority (CDA) has completed the recruitment process for three new directors general (DGs) in BS-20.

According to CDA officials, retired Brig Mohammad Javed Iqbal, retired Brig Rashid Manzoor and retired Brig Azhar Khan have been appointed as DGs.

The newly appointed officers have been assigned different departments, according to notifications issued by the CDA. Retired Brig Javed Iqbal has been posted as Director General Civic Management, while retired Brig Rashid Manzoor has been appointed DG Planning and Development.

Similarly, retired Brig Azhar Khan has been posted as DG Land and Estate Management.

The new DGs have initially been appointed on a contract basis for two years, with the possibility of an extension subject to satisfactory performance.

“Yes, our process of appointing DGs has been completed, and new officers have been posted to important positions to improve the working of the CDA,” an authority official said.

Asked about the recruitment process, the official said the appointments had been made through a competitive selection process.

“After the advertisement, around 100 shortlisted candidates were interviewed, and following a rigorous process, the three officers in question were selected,” he said, adding that the advertisement had stated that retired commissioned officers in BS-20 would be given preference.

“The new DGs are competent and thorough professionals, and their induction will improve the working of the CDA,” he added.

According to the advertisement issued in April this year, the CDA had invited applications from candidates with 16 years of education and 25 years of experience in the government sector for the posts of DGs. The advertisement had stated that retired commissioned officers in BS-20 would be preferred.

The CDA had planned to complete the recruitment process in May-June. However, litigation delayed the process. In May, the Islamabad High Court (IHC) granted a stay on the recruitment process following a petition filed by Iftikhar Haideri, a BS-19 officer of the CDA, who had approached the court after the civic agency did not promote him.

He had stated that the Departmental Promotion Committee (DPC) had recommended his promotion from BS-19 to BS-20, but he was not promoted despite the recommendation. He had also pleaded that the BS-20 positions of DGs in the CDA were meant to be filled through promotions and that direct recruitment could not be made against them.

However, after the stay was vacated, the CDA completed the recruitment process and issued notifications appointing the new DGs.

Meanwhile, in a related development, the CDA transferred BS-20 officer Abdul Razzaq from the post of DG Civic Management a few days ago and directed him to report to the authority’s Human Resource Department.

CDA officials said a DG Law would also be appointed soon through a competitive selection process on a contract basis.

Published in Dawn, November 2nd, 2026

headline: Police set up eight pickets for PAF base security in Rawalpindi
description: As part of the security plan, police mobile squads will patrol around Nur Khan PAF Base.
author: Mohammad Asghar
article_text:
RAWALPINDI: Eight special police pickets have been set up at various locations to ensure the security of the PAF base.

A separate police picket with 40 officers has also been set up at Azad Patan to guarantee the safety of important establishments and prevent any untoward incidents.

According to police sources, the special police picket at Azad Patan has been established with the deployment of 40 police personnel, headed by a superintendent of police (SP), who will be responsible for briefing the personnel and ensuring their presence at the picket.

The police have been deployed at Azad Patan in two shifts. A police reserve team equipped with anti-riot equipment has been placed on standby at the Kahuta police station.

The eight police pickets were established on Saturday until further orders. They have been set up at Khokhar Road, Chaklala Stand, Chhtari Chowk, Shaheen Chowk, TNT Chowk, TM Chowk, GPO Chowk and Hali Road.

As part of the security plan for the eight pickets, police mobile squads from Chaklala, Sadiqabad and Waris Khan police stations will patrol around Nur Khan PAF Base, while the Muhafiz Squad and Dolphin Force have been assigned patrol duties around the base.

At the TM Chowk police picket, the RA Bazaar police, Muhafiz Squad and Dolphin Force will patrol within the limits of the R.A. Bazaar police station.

Published in Dawn, November 2nd, 2026

headline: Man sentenced to life for assaulting minor sister-in-law
description: PHC accepts appeal of victim, sets aside acquittal order of trial court.
author: Waseem Ahmad Shah
article_text:
PESHAWAR: Peshawar High Court has set aside the acquittal of a medical doctor and sentenced him to life imprisonment with fine of Rs500,000 for sexually assaulting his 12-year-old sister-in-law over three years ago.

A bench consisting of Justice Sahibzada Asadullah and Justice Inamullah Khan accepted an appeal filed by the victim and declared that the trial court had erred in acquitting the suspect.

The bench convicted the man under Section 376 of Pakistan Penal Code and Section 53 of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Child Protection and Welfare Act. The convict was sentenced to life imprisonment with a fine of Rs500,000 under Section 376-B of PPC.

Similarly, he was sentenced under Section 53 of CPWA to seven years rigorous imprisonment, along with a fine of Rs100,000. The bench ordered that both the sentences should run concurrently.

PHC accepts appeal of victim, sets aside acquittal order of trial court

An additional sessions judge/child protection court had acquitted the suspect on Nov 11, 2025 in the case. He was charged in an FIR registered at Hayatabad police station on Feb 14, 2023, over a complaint lodged by the victim, who had visited the station along with her father.

The complainant and her father are also US nationals and had gone there after the occurrence. The wife of the suspect (sister of the victim) had also taken divorce from him afterward. The victim and her father had recorded their statements during trial from the US through video link.

According to the prosecution, the occurrence took place on Feb 6, 2023. The victim claimed in the FIR that her parents and sister had gone outside for some work, while her brother was asleep in the guest room of the house. She claimed that she was present in the lounge, when the suspect approached her and sexually assaulted her.

Barrister Amir Khan Chamkani appeared for the appellant and contended that despite presence of sufficient evidence connecting the suspect with the commission of the offence, the trial court had acquitted him.

The counsel for the respondent attributed the prosecution case to a conspiracy, contending that the alleged victim’s sister, who was married to the respondent, desired dissolution of the marriage and that, to facilitate such separation, the victim’s family fabricated the present allegation and falsely implicated his client.

The bench overruled his arguments, observing that the mere fact that a matrimonial dispute subsequently arose between the respondent and his wife didn’t establish that the present criminal allegation was conceived or engineered for the purpose of facilitating dissolution of that marriage.

In its 39-page detailed judgement, the bench discussed multiple aspects of the case including delay of eight days in lodging the complaint and forensic evidence available on the record.

“The victim’s father was admittedly abroad at the relevant time; the victim remained within the family environment; the accused was closely related to her in different capacities; and, upon his return to the country, the father furnished his passport and boarding pass to the investigating officer, thereby providing contemporaneous material supporting his absence and subsequent arrival,” the bench ruled.

“The record, therefore, does not present a case of unexplained or suspicious silence. Rather, it reflects a short interval arising in the context of an allegation of an exceptionally grave and sensitive nature, involving a closely connected family member, in circumstances where the victim and her family were confronted with the immediate consequences of the occurrence and were required to decide how and when to set the criminal law in motion,” the bench observed.

It added that the mere lapse of eight days couldn’t, in such circumstances, be treated as conclusive proof of consultation, deliberation or fabrication on part of the complainant.

“The approach adopted by the learned trial court is also inconsistent with the settled judicial understanding of human behaviour in cases involving sexual offences.

Delay in reporting such an occurrence cannot be assessed through an inflexible or stereotypical standard of conduct, divorced from the social, familial and psychological circumstances in which the allegation arises,” the bench ruled.

Referring to different judgements of superior courts, the bench pointed out: “The Supreme Court of Pakistan has repeatedly recognised that the victim and her family may require time to recover from the shock of the occurrence and to overcome the stigma, shame and apprehension associated with reporting a sexual offence.”

The bench referred to one of the judgements wherein it was observed that prevailing social taboos might result in cases of rape remaining unreported and that a victim could not be disbelieved merely on account of an ostensible delay in reporting the occurrence. The bench also discussed the forensic evidence in the case.

“In the present case, the DNA profiling was conducted by the duly constituted forensic laboratory; the samples and their examination have been established through the prosecution evidence; and no substantive circumstance has been brought on record to impeach the integrity, authenticity or scientific methodology of the laboratory examination,” the bench pointed out.

“The approach adopted by the learned trial court is also inconsistent with the settled judicial understanding of human behaviour in cases involving sexual offences.

“In the present case, the DNA profiling was conducted by the duly constituted forensic laboratory; the samples and their examination have been established through the prosecution evidence; and no substantive circumstance has been brought on record to impeach the integrity, authenticity or scientific methodology of the laboratory examination,” the bench pointed out.

headline: KP doctors oppose amendments to Pharmacy Act 1967
description: Legislation would curtail medical practitioners’ authority to prescribe and dispense medicines to patients.
author: Our Correspondent
article_text:
MANSEHRA: Doctors across Khyber Pakhtunkhwa have opposed any legislation or amendments to the Pharmacy Act 1967 that would curtail medical practitioners’ authority to prescribe and dispense medicines to patients.

“We will never accept amendments to the PMDC Act 2022, laws governing registered medical practitioners, the Drugs Rules and Minimum Service Delivery Standards (MSDS) of the Punjab and the federal territory, or any infringement on the professional domains of provincial healthcare commissions and patients’ legal rights,” Dr Mohammad Rizwan Rajpot, vice-chairman of the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Professional Doctors Association, told reporters here on Sunday.

He said a delegation of senior doctors from Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, including Dr Zulfiqar Ali, Dr Hakeem Khan Marwat and Dr Khawaj Abid, met members of the National Assembly’s Standing Committee on National Health Services, Regulations and Coordination in Islamabad last week and conveyed their reservations about the proposed amendments to independent prescribing rules.

“The proposed amendment seeking to abolish Section 31 (4) of the Pharmacy Act 1967 is unacceptable to doctors, as it empowers registered medical practitioners to independently prescribe, dispense and supply medicines to patients at their clinics and hospitals. The PMDC upholds this authority in its rules and licensing framework,” Dr Rizwan said.

He said that the delegation led by him also raised concerns over the alleged appointment and frequent promotions of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Deputy Secretary Drugs Mohammad Ibrahim.

“We want the NA’s high-level standing committee to investigate and hold accountable anyone responsible for discrepancies and misuse of authority and recommend punitive action if tampering with public documents is established,” Dr Rizwan said.

He added that the delegation had also asked the prime minister to order an inquiry into Category-B health education institutions in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa to identify alleged irregularities in the awarding of degrees.

Dr Rizwan said Dr Shaista and other members of the National Assembly’s Standing Committee on National Health Services assured the delegation that its concerns would be taken up in their meeting for remedial measures accordingly.

Published in Dawn, November 2nd, 2026

headline: Saudi strikes on port, oil facility in Yemen wound 7: Houthis
description: Yemen’s Houthis said Monday that Saudi strikes targeted a key Red Sea port and oil facility in Hodeidah province,...
article_text:
Yemen’s Houthis said that Saudi strikes targeted a key Red Sea port and oil facility in Hodeidah province, wounding seven people.

The Iran-backed group is fighting a Saudi-led coalition supporting Yemen’s internationally recognised government after a civil war reignited in one of the world’s poorest countries.

Saudi-coalition strikes on Ras Issa port wounded four civilians, while three more were hurt in an attack on an oil facility in Bajil district, Houthi health ministry spokesman Anees Alasbahi said in a post on X.

headline: Governor Kundi says Centre failing to give KP support it deserves
description: Says collective efforts needed to restore province’s positive image.
author: Bureau Report
article_text:
PESHAWAR: Governor Faisal Karim Kundi has said that the federal government is failing to provide Khyber Pakhtunkhwa the support it deserves.

Addressing the annual conference of Pakistan Association of Urological Surgeons here on Sunday, he said that ignoring KP must be brought to an end without further delay. He said that practical steps were required to improve the province’s health sector on the pattern of Punjab and Sindh.

He said that medical conferences provided an important platform for promotion of knowledge, research, exchange of experiences and awareness about modern treatment methods, according to a statement.

The governor stressed the need for ensuring quality and specialised healthcare services in merged districts, southern districts and far-flung areas of the province. He said that modern treatment facilities should not remain limited to big cities and every citizen must have equal access to healthcare.

Says collective efforts needed to restore province’s positive image

He stated that improvement of health infrastructure, provision of modern medical equipment, doctors’ training and promotion of medical research were essential for strengthening healthcare system.

The governor said that professional organisations like Pakistan Association of Urological Surgeons could play a vital role in enhancing doctors’ capacity, training young medical experts and developing collaboration with public sector hospitals.

He said the Rs70,000 monthly salary of house officers was insufficient and it would be reviewed.

Meanwhile, during his address at Darbar-i-Aalia Murshadabad Sharif in the provincial capital, the governor said that lasting peace was essential for the province’s progress and prosperity.

He stressed the need for collective contribution of all segments of the society for promoting positive image of the province.

Mr Kundi said that religious scholars had a vital role to play in promoting peace, unity and harmony across the province. He added that ulema should use their influence to spread the message of tolerance, discourage extremism and support collective efforts for lasting peace in the province.

In a statement issued from his office, the governor emphasised the need for unity, lasting peace, development, promotion of sports, effective utilisation of the province’s natural resources and collective efforts to ensure welfare and prosperity of the people.

The ceremony was attended by former prime minister Shahid Khaqan Abbasi, governor’s adviser Tayab Qureshi and others, read an official statement.

Mr Kundi said that the province had endured decades of terrorism and rendered immense sacrifices, with religious scholars, security personnel, politicians and innocent students, including the martyrs of Army Public School, laying down their lives for peace.

He said that peace was the basic requirement for development. He said that the province was known for its resilience in the face of terrorism and was now determined to move towards lasting stability and progress.

He said that KP had produced outstanding sportspersons from Mardan, Dera Ismail Khan and Bannu who had won international recognition. He said that youth should be provided with opportunities to excel in sports and other fields.

He stated that the province was blessed with abundant natural resources including oil, gas, water resources, tourism potential and the Tarbela Dam, which could transform its economy if properly utilised.

Recalling Peshawar’s past reputation as the ‘city of flowers’, the governor said that collective efforts were required to restore the province’s positive image.

“Safety of our people comes first, followed by the development of the province and the progress of the country,” he said, adding that the province would witness significant positive change in the near future.

He congratulated the newly-graduated Huffaz, distributed certificates among them, visited the institution’s library and appreciated its services in the field of education.

article_html:
PESHAWAR: Governor Faisal Karim Kundi has said that the federal government is failing to provide Khyber Pakhtunkhwa the support it deserves.

Addressing the annual conference of Pakistan Association of Urological Surgeons here on Sunday, he said that ignoring KP must be brought to an end without further delay. He said that practical steps were required to improve the province’s health sector on the pattern of Punjab and Sindh.

He said that medical conferences provided an important platform for promotion of knowledge, research, exchange of experiences and awareness about modern treatment methods, according to a statement.

The governor stressed the need for ensuring quality and specialised healthcare services in merged districts, southern districts and far-flung areas of the province. He said that modern treatment facilities should not remain limited to big cities and every citizen must have equal access to healthcare.

Says collective efforts needed to restore province’s positive image

He stated that improvement of health infrastructure, provision of modern medical equipment, doctors’ training and promotion of medical research were essential for strengthening healthcare system.

The governor said that professional organisations like Pakistan Association of Urological Surgeons could play a vital role in enhancing doctors’ capacity, training young medical experts and developing collaboration with public sector hospitals.

He said the Rs70,000 monthly salary of house officers was insufficient and it would be reviewed.

Meanwhile, during his address at Darbar-i-Aalia Murshadabad Sharif in the provincial capital, the governor said that lasting peace was essential for the province’s progress and prosperity.

He stressed the need for collective contribution of all segments of the society for promoting positive image of the province.

Mr Kundi said that religious scholars had a vital role to play in promoting peace, unity and harmony across the province. He added that ulema should use their influence to spread the message of tolerance, discourage extremism and support collective efforts for lasting peace in the province.

In a statement issued from his office, the governor emphasised the need for unity, lasting peace, development, promotion of sports, effective utilisation of the province’s natural resources and collective efforts to ensure welfare and prosperity of the people.

The ceremony was attended by former prime minister Shahid Khaqan Abbasi, governor’s adviser Tayab Qureshi and others, read an official statement.

Mr Kundi said that the province had endured decades of terrorism and rendered immense sacrifices, with religious scholars, security personnel, politicians and innocent students, including the martyrs of Army Public School, laying down their lives for peace.

He said that peace was the basic requirement for development. He said that the province was known for its resilience in the face of terrorism and was now determined to move towards lasting stability and progress.

He said that KP had produced outstanding sportspersons from Mardan, Dera Ismail Khan and Bannu who had won international recognition. He said that youth should be provided with opportunities to excel in sports and other fields.

He stated that the province was blessed with abundant natural resources including oil, gas, water resources, tourism potential and the Tarbela Dam, which could transform its economy if properly utilised.

Recalling Peshawar’s past reputation as the ‘city of flowers’, the governor said that collective efforts were required to restore the province’s positive image.

“Safety of our people comes first, followed by the development of the province and the progress of the country,” he said, adding that the province would witness significant positive change in the near future.

He congratulated the newly-graduated Huffaz, distributed certificates among them, visited the institution’s library and appreciated its services in the field of education.

Published in Dawn, November 2nd, 2026

headline: Nine people dead in Learjet crash in south Florida, officials say
description: Videos on social ​media show the jet slamming into the ground next to a road and exploding.
author: Reuters
article_text:
A Learjet crashed on Sunday afternoon in a residential area in Palm Beach County, Florida, ‌killing all nine people on board, US transportation officials said.

The private jet had taken off from Austin-Bergstrom International Airport in Texas and was headed to North Eleuthera Airport in the Bahamas, the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) said in a statement.

Videos on social ​media showed the jet slamming into the ground next to a road and exploding.

“It was a ​big-time tragedy that happened,” Florida Governor Ron DeSantis said at a press conference near ⁠the crash site in Lake Worth Beach.

“When you see that video, it’s a jarring thing. It was like ​a missile coming down, and a massive explosion, debris going everywhere.”

The National Transportation Safety Board said it had ​launched an investigation into the crash, which Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy called a “horrific tragedy”.

FAA records list the Bombardier-made Learjet 60’s owner as a Delaware corporation. Canada-based Bombardier said it would fully support the investigation and cooperate as needed.

The crash left a “massive crater” ​by the road near the entrance to a mobile home park, Palm Beach County Commissioner Joel Flores ​said at the news conference. About 600 people were being evacuated from the area and relocated to two shelters in the ‌county, ⁠Flores said.

Heavy rainfall and thunderstorms were occurring in the area at the time, forecaster AccuWeather said in a statement.

An audio recording from a Miami air traffic control centre posted on LiveATC, a site that broadcasts air traffic control communications, captured the plane’s final moments before the crash in unusual detail.

At first, someone in the plane’s ​cockpit reported to an ​air traffic controller that ⁠they were “managing the ice” but faced “moderate” turbulence and were seeking “better rides”.

Less than a minute later, the person said “Mayday, mayday”, reporting that the plane was suddenly descending at a ​rate of 10,000 feet per minute.

Seconds later, the person said they were declaring ​an emergency, ⁠with the rate of descent accelerating to 20,000 feet per minute.

Less than 20 seconds later, the person said: “We’re going to crash into the ground” before saying that the descent rate had reached 22,000 feet per minute as the ⁠plane started ​banking.

About 35 seconds after the initial mayday announcement, the last thing ​heard from the cockpit was a rapidly spoken “We’re out of time”.

Flight tracking website Flightradar24 said data showed the vertical descent rate at ​one point exceeded 32,000 feet per minute.
