LAHORE: The Punjab government on Monday informed the Lahore High Court (LHC) that a civilian who commits an offence against the state and is convicted cannot claim the protection of fundamental rights.

The response came as the government sought the dismissal of a petition filed by Barrister Hassaan Khan Niazi, nephew of PTI founder Imran Khan, challenging his handover to the army and subsequent trial in a case related to the May 9 riots.

In a report submitted after almost a year on behalf of the provincial government through the home secretary and the inspector general of police, the deputy inspector general of police (legal) said every citizen’s first duty was loyalty to the state, citing a 2005 LHC judgment (PLD 2005 LAH 721).

The report described Niazi as a convicted prisoner, arguing that his release through a second round of litigation, other than by way of appeal, was not permissible.

It said no judicial order was required for his handover because Niazi was neither in judicial custody nor on remand.

The report further stated that he was an absconder, unlike the 16 co-accused whose transfer had been sought from an anti-terrorism court while they were in jail.

The Sarwar Road station house officer neither handed over Niazi’s custody nor received a letter from the commanding officer, the report added.

“That was done by the investigation in-charge of the Sarwar Road police station, who is not a party to the petition,” the report claimed.

It stated that the Supreme Court’s May 7, 2025, ruling on the intra-court appeals upheld military trials while granting the accused the right to appeal, but not the right to file constitutional petitions.

It said Niazi had already filed an appeal under Section 133-B of the Pakistan Army Act, 1952.

“It is a well-established principle that the same question of law cannot be challenged in two different forums simultaneously; therefore, this petition lacks maintainability in the eyes of the law,” the report maintained.

It further argued that Niazi had misread the Supreme Court’s short order, which applied only to petitions pending or filed against anti-terrorism court orders.

It accused him of concealing facts about his appeal, his father Hafeezullah Khan Niazi’s earlier proceedings, including a petition before the apex court and a contempt petition, as well as the anti-terrorism court’s May 25, 2023, order.

The report said Niazi had not annexed the military court’s order, an objection upheld by the high court in two other petitions.

It prayed the court to dismiss the petition on the grounds that it was devoid of merit and not maintainable.

According to the report, Niazi was a proclaimed offender in FIR No. 96/2023, registered on May 10, 2023, at the Sarwar Road police station in Lahore Cantonment in connection with an attack on Jinnah House, which was also the residence of the Lahore Corps commander.

Police arrested Niazi in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa on Aug 16, 2023. The next day, the commanding officer of the 54 Electrical and Mechanical Engineers Battalion, Lahore, asked for his custody, saying his alleged offences fell under the Official Secrets Act, 1923 and the Pakistan Army Act, 1952 and were triable by court-martial.

Police handed him over under Section 76 of the Army Act, read with Section 549(3) of the Code of Criminal Procedure. He was later sentenced to ten years’ imprisonment in December 2024.

Defence ministry’s reply

The defence ministry told the LHC that Niazi went to Jinnah House on May 9, 2023, where he made videos and passed sarcastic remarks about the Corps Commander’s uniform.

“The incident impacted the image of Pakistan and was prejudicial to the safety and interest of the state,” said a reply signed by an assistant judge advocate general, the army’s legal branch at Headquarters 4 Corps, and filed through an additional attorney general.

The reply said that Niazi, held at Kot Lakhpat Jail, was convicted by a Field General Court Martial (FGCM) and sentenced to 10 years’ rigorous imprisonment under Section 3 of the Official Secrets Act, 1923, read with Section 59 of the Army Act.

It argued that the petition was barred by Articles 199(3) and 8(3) of the Constitution, xcludes matters related to the proceedings of the armed forces personnel from the purview of the high courts, and that Niazi already had an appeal pending under Section 133-B of the Army Act before the army court of appeals.

It said the SC’s May 7, 2025 short order restored Sections 2(1)(d) and 59(4) of the Army Act without striking down Section 133-B.

The direction that high courts decide petitions “on their own merits”, the reply said, is not a blanket exemption from the constitutional bar. It said Niazi was tried with a counsel of his choice and made a judicial confession before a magistrate that he did not retract at trial.

It said the trial ended on Jan 5, 2024 and he was admitted to Lahore’s Central Jail on Dec 26, 2024. It also argued that he had waited nearly two years before coming to court.

The defence ministry’s reply pointed out that Niazi was taken into military custody under Section 549(3) of the Code of Criminal Procedure.

It denied discrimination under Article 25, saying that protesters involved in ordinary disruption were tried by the antiterrorism courts, whereas Niazi’s alleged offence involved a prohibited military installation.

A joint trial with the ordinary accused was legally impossible, it said, adding that no Official Secrets Act case had gone to an ordinary court so far.

It added that weekly phone calls and meetings with Niazi’s family were arranged after the handover.

The ministry asked the court to dismiss the petition as premature, not maintainable and without merit, pleading that the Constitution barred the high court from hearing cases involving persons subject to the Pakistan Army Act, 1952.

headline: TotalEnergies expects Iran war to accelerate energy transition
description: French oil major TotalEnergies expects global oil demand to peak in the years between 2035 and 2040, with potential...
article_text:
French oil major TotalEnergies expects global oil demand to peak in the years between 2035 and 2040, with potential for demand to decline faster if sales of electric vehicles continue to grow, Reuters reports citing the company’s chief sustainability officer.

The company’s annual energy outlook report projects that global demand for petroleum products will increase and plateau during the 2030s before beginning a slow decline. Last year’s forecast had expected oil demand to rise until 2040 before declining gradually.

The report adds that the crisis in energy markets triggered by the US-Israeli war on Iran could, however, act as an “accelerator” of the energy transition, pointing to a sharp increase in EV sales in Asia, Latin America and Europe, and an increase in biofuel blending requirements influencing energy consumption patterns.

Chief sustainability officer Aurelien Hamelle tells reporters there has been a “stunning acceleration” of low-carbon technology between the second quarter of 2025 and the second quarter of 2026.

headline: Govt enlists oil refineries to shield citizens from global price hikes
description: Says they will bear a burden of Rs15bn, which will allow petrol to be sold at Rs15 less than the global market.
author: News Desk
article_text:
The government announced on Monday that oil refineries would bear a burden of approximately Rs15 billion each month, which would allow petrol to be sold Rs15 cheaper than what it was in the global market amid the US-Israeli war on Iran.

The announcement came at a press conference in Islamabad addressed by Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik and Information Minister Attaullah Tarar.

Addressing the conference, Malik said that the premier had made efforts to meet with refineries and consult with them regarding interventions to ensure that people got the cheapest petrol amid impending steep fuel price increases, including an increase of about Rs15 that would have taken effect on Friday.

“I am grateful to all the refineries that saw the public is in difficulty and with the government’s help … increased their throughput,” the minister said, adding that these refineries had made profits from this throughput in the last three months.

“They were requested to take a step to support the public during this difficult time, and I am glad that they listened to us … the Rs15 increase that was coming in the petrol prices on Friday, they helped the government with that and because of that we were able to maintain the price.”

He added that more improvement would be seen by the public, expressing his gratitude to the refineries for standing with the government to provide assistance to the public during a time that had caused everyone difficulties — even the government as it struggled to procure oil at increasing prices.

As a result of this step, he highlighted, a load of approximately Rs15 billion a month would be borne by these refineries, allowing petrol to be sold at a rate Rs15 per litre cheaper than what it would be in the international market.

He expressed his hope that the crisis in the Middle East would soon move towards a peace agreement and that the government could advance with its purposes of “taking the system towards improvement, deregulation and refinery upgrades”.

“The government doesn’t want to be cruel to anyone,” Malik stressed, saying that it intended to take actions “with consultations, keeping the public’s interests in mind, in a fair way”.

He added that before the crisis, the premium of the refineries was $5 per barrel, and even today a $20 limit had been established. He further said that the government would have to step in and protect the public in case of further difficulties.

Tarar also addressed the conference, noting that the premier’s vision “from the first day” had been to put as little burden on the country as possible.

He said that even though the situation in the Middle East had affected every economy, including that of Pakistan, “our macroeconomic indicators have remained largely stable — Pakistan’s economy hasn’t taken as much of a hit as other countries”.

Regarding Friday’s situation, when petrol prices were increasing in the international market, he said that PM Shehbaz had directed refineries to absorb the price hike in order to prevent the Rs15 increase.

“During this difficult time … I think this is a great effort, as a result of which the public has been saved from this difficulty,” the information minister said.

He also discussed the fuel subsidy scheme, saying, “If you told me two months ago that there would be a scheme in which, upon SMS registration, motorcycle users get a weekly concession of Rs500 on petrol, and 800cc car users, every 10 days, get 10 litres of petrol for Rs100 less per litre, then I would have told you that it’s probably not possible to implement such a scheme.”

He praised PM Shehbaz’s “will power, intent and empathy for the public” that served as the foundation for the scheme.

Tarar highlighted that the number of unique users who had registered for the scheme had now crossed 15 million. He said that about Rs27bn had so far been allocated towards this relief and highlighted its success.

“This is a unique relief that is not available in the rest of the world,” he said, referring to both the fuel subsidy scheme and the steps taken by the government to prevent the increase in prices on Friday.

Answering questions, Malik said that he was the “biggest advocate for deregulation” and for bringing competition into sectors, seeing it as the way to protect people’s welfare and deliver good service. However, he pointed out, “Have you seen any incident in the last 50 years that has been happening in the last six to eight months? What rules-based order do you want to adopt in the middle of this disaster?”

He stressed that once the crisis in the region ended, the government would make efforts to return to deregulation; however, currently the focus was on public relief.

More to follow

article_html:
The government announced on Monday that oil refineries would bear a burden of approximately Rs15 billion each month, which would allow petrol to be sold Rs15 cheaper than what it was in the global market amid the US-Israeli war on Iran.

The announcement came at a press conference in Islamabad addressed by Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik and Information Minister Attaullah Tarar.

Addressing the conference, Malik said that the premier had made efforts to meet with refineries and consult with them regarding interventions to ensure that people got the cheapest petrol amid impending steep fuel price increases, including an increase of about Rs15 that would have taken effect on Friday.

“I am grateful to all the refineries that saw the public is in difficulty and with the government’s help … increased their throughput,” the minister said, adding that these refineries had made profits from this throughput in the last three months.

“They were requested to take a step to support the public during this difficult time, and I am glad that they listened to us … the Rs15 increase that was coming in the petrol prices on Friday, they helped the government with that and because of that we were able to maintain the price.”

He added that more improvement would be seen by the public, expressing his gratitude to the refineries for standing with the government to provide assistance to the public during a time that had caused everyone difficulties — even the government as it struggled to procure oil at increasing prices.

As a result of this step, he highlighted, a load of approximately Rs15 billion a month would be borne by these refineries, allowing petrol to be sold at a rate Rs15 per litre cheaper than what it would be in the international market.

He expressed his hope that the crisis in the Middle East would soon move towards a peace agreement and that the government could advance with its purposes of “taking the system towards improvement, deregulation and refinery upgrades”.

“The government doesn’t want to be cruel to anyone,” Malik stressed, saying that it intended to take actions “with consultations, keeping the public’s interests in mind, in a fair way”.

He added that before the crisis, the premium of the refineries was $5 per barrel, and even today a $20 limit had been established. He further said that the government would have to step in and protect the public in case of further difficulties.

Tarar also addressed the conference, noting that the premier’s vision “from the first day” had been to put as little burden on the country as possible.

He said that even though the situation in the Middle East had affected every economy, including that of Pakistan, “our macroeconomic indicators have remained largely stable — Pakistan’s economy hasn’t taken as much of a hit as other countries”.

Regarding Friday’s situation, when petrol prices were increasing in the international market, he said that PM Shehbaz had directed refineries to absorb the price hike in order to prevent the Rs15 increase.

“During this difficult time … I think this is a great effort, as a result of which the public has been saved from this difficulty,” the information minister said.

He also discussed the fuel subsidy scheme, saying, “If you told me two months ago that there would be a scheme in which, upon SMS registration, motorcycle users get a weekly concession of Rs500 on petrol, and 800cc car users, every 10 days, get 10 litres of petrol for Rs100 less per litre, then I would have told you that it’s probably not possible to implement such a scheme.”

He praised PM Shehbaz’s “will power, intent and empathy for the public” that served as the foundation for the scheme.

Tarar highlighted that the number of unique users who had registered for the scheme had now crossed 15 million. He said that about Rs27bn had so far been allocated towards this relief and highlighted its success.

“This is a unique relief that is not available in the rest of the world,” he said, referring to both the fuel subsidy scheme and the steps taken by the government to prevent the increase in prices on Friday.

Answering questions, Malik said that he was the “biggest advocate for deregulation” and for bringing competition into sectors, seeing it as the way to protect people’s welfare and deliver good service. However, he pointed out, “Have you seen any incident in the last 50 years that has been happening in the last six to eight months? What rules-based order do you want to adopt in the middle of this disaster?”

He stressed that once the crisis in the region ended, the government would make efforts to return to deregulation; however, currently the focus was on public relief.

More to follow
